options.text: The process of cell division
A type of sexual reproduction
A change in the base sequence of DNA
The transfer of genes between organisms

questions.explanation: A mutation is a change in the base sequence of DNA. Mutations can occur randomly and spontaneously during DNA replication, or can be caused by environmental factors called mutagens.

questions.stem: Which type of gene mutation involves one base being replaced by a different base?

options.text: Deletion
Translocation
Substitution
Insertion

questions.explanation: A substitution mutation is when one base in the DNA sequence is replaced by a different base. This may change one amino acid in the protein, but does not affect the reading of subsequent codons.

questions.stem: Why are insertion and deletion mutations often more harmful than substitution mutations?

options.text: Because they only occur in sex cells
Because they cause a frameshift, changing every subsequent amino acid
Because they are caused by radiation
Because they always cause cancer

questions.explanation: Insertion and deletion mutations cause a frameshift, meaning all the codons after the mutation are read differently. This changes every subsequent amino acid in the protein, usually making it completely non-functional.

options.text: A gene that controls mutation rate
An organism that has undergone a mutation
An environmental factor that increases the rate of mutation
A type of protein produced by mutated DNA

questions.explanation: A mutagen is an environmental factor that increases the rate of mutation. Examples include UV radiation, X-rays, and certain chemicals such as those found in cigarette smoke.

options.text: Always harmful and cause disease
Neutral, having no effect on the organism
Only found in plants
Always beneficial

questions.explanation: Most mutations are neutral and have no effect on the organism. This is often because they occur in non-coding regions of DNA, or the change still codes for the same amino acid due to the redundancy of the genetic code.

questions.stem: For a mutation to be inherited by offspring, it must occur in:

options.text: Red blood cells
Sex cells (gametes)
Any body cell
Skin cells

questions.explanation: For a mutation to be passed to offspring, it must occur in sex cells (gametes) such as sperm or egg cells. Mutations in body cells (somatic mutations) affect only that individual and are not inherited.

questions.stem: Why are mutations described as the ultimate source of genetic variation?

options.text: Because they only occur during sexual reproduction
Because they happen more often than meiosis
Because they always improve an organism's fitness
Because they create new alleles that did not previously exist

questions.explanation: Mutations are the ultimate source of genetic variation because they create entirely new alleles. While meiosis and sexual reproduction shuffle existing alleles, only mutations produce new genetic information for natural selection to act upon.
